entries.d28242ff69c68cf1848dfa5b0c4203c50ab5abeb: <div sID="gen7675" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="6" osisID="1Chr.6" sID="1Chr.6"/> <div eID="gen7675" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7676" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen7677" type="x-p"/> Though Joseph and Judah shared between them the forfeited honours of the birthright, yet Levi was first of all the tribes, dignified and distinguished with an honour more valuable than either the precedency or the double portion, and that was the priesthood. That tribe God set apart for himself; it was Moses's tribe, and perhaps for his sake was thus favoured. Of that tribe we have an account in this chapter. I. Their pedigree, the first fathers of the tribe (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1-1Chr.6.3">ver. 1-3</reference>), the line of the priests, from Aaron to the captivity (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.4-1Chr.6.15">ver. 4-15</reference>), and of some other of their families, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16-1Chr.6.30">ver. 16-30</reference>. II. Their work, the work of the Levites (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.31-1Chr.6.48">ver. 31-48</reference>), of the priests, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.49-1Chr.6.53">ver. 49-53</reference>. III. The cities appointed them in the land of Canaan, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.54-1Chr.6.81">ver. 54-81</reference>.
entries.0e13f63d5c953488f69f170366b35a90f47c9a1e: <div eID="gen7677" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen7676" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">Genealogies. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1450.)</title> <div sID="gen7678" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> The sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. <hi type="super">2</hi> And the sons of Kohath; Amram, Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel. <hi type="super">3</hi> And the children of Amram; Aaron, and Moses, and Miriam. The sons also of Aaron; Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. <hi type="super">4</hi> Eleazar begat Phinehas, Phinehas begat Abishua, <hi type="super">5</hi> And Abishua begat Bukki, and Bukki begat Uzzi, <hi type="super">6</hi> And Uzzi begat Zerahiah, and Zerahiah begat Meraioth, <hi type="super">7</hi> Meraioth begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub, <hi type="super">8</hi> And Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Ahimaaz, <hi type="super">9</hi> And Ahimaaz begat Azariah, and Azariah begat Johanan, <hi type="super">10</hi> And Johanan begat Azariah, (he <hi type="italic">it is</hi> that executed the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem:) <hi type="super">11</hi> And Azariah begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub, <hi type="super">12</hi> And Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Shallum, <hi type="super">13</hi> And Shallum begat Hilkiah, and Hilkiah begat Azariah, <hi type="super">14</hi> And Azariah begat Seraiah, and Seraiah begat Jehozadak, <hi type="super">15</hi> And Jehozadak went <hi type="italic">into captivity,</hi> when the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> carried away Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. <hi type="super">16</hi> The sons of Levi; Gershom, Kohath, and Merari. <hi type="super">17</hi> And these <hi type="italic">be</hi> the names of the sons of Gershom; Libni, and Shimei. <hi type="super">18</hi> And the sons of Kohath <hi type="italic">were,</hi> Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel. <hi type="super">19</hi> The sons of Merari; Mahli, and Mushi. And these <hi type="italic">are</hi> the families of the Levites according to their fathers. <hi type="super">20</hi> Of Gershom; Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son, <hi type="super">21</hi> Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeaterai his son. <hi type="super">22</hi> The sons of Kohath; Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son, <hi type="super">23</hi> Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son, <hi type="super">24</hi> Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son. <hi type="super">25</hi> And the sons of Elkanah; Amasai, and Ahimoth. <hi type="super">26</hi> <hi type="italic">As for</hi> Elkanah: the sons of Elkanah; Zophai his son, and Nahath his son, <hi type="super">27</hi> Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son. <hi type="super">28</hi> And the sons of Samuel; the firstborn Vashni, and Abiah. <hi type="super">29</hi> The sons of Merari; Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzza his son, <hi type="super">30</hi> Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son. <div eID="gen7678" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7679" type="x-p"/> The priests and Levites were more concerned than any other Israelites to preserve their pedigree clear and to be able to prove it, because all the honours and privileges of their office depended upon their descent. And we read of those who, though perhaps they really were children of the priests, yet, because they could not find the register of their genealogies, nor make out their descent by any authentic record, were, <hi type="italic">as polluted, put from the priesthood,</hi> and forbidden to eat of the holy things, <reference osisRef="Ezra.2.62-Ezra.2.63">Ezra ii. 62, 63</reference>. It is but very little that is here recorded of the genealogies of this sacred tribe. I. The first fathers of it are here named twice, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">v. 1</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16">16</reference>. Gershom, Kohath, and Merari, are three names which we were very conversant with in the book of Numbers, when the families of the Levites were marshalled and had their work assigned to them. Aaron, and Moses, and Miriam, we have known much more of than their names, and cannot pass them over here without remembering that this was that Moses and Aaron whom God honoured in making them instruments of Israel's deliverance and settlement and <hi type="italic">figures of him that was to come,</hi> Moses as a prophet and Aaron as a priest. And the mention of Nadab and Abihu (though, having no children, there was no occasion to bring them into the genealogy) cannot but remind us of the terrors of that divine justice which they were made monuments of for offering strange fire, that we may always fear before him. 2. The line of Eleazar, the successor of Aaron, is here drawn down to the time of the captivity, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.4-1Chr.6.15">v. 4-15</reference>. It begins with Eleazar, who came out of the house of bondage in Egypt, and ends with Jehozadak, who went into the house of bondage in Babylon. Thus, for their sins, they were left as they were found, which might also intimate that the Levitical priesthood did not make anything perfect, but this was to be done by the <hi type="italic">bringing in of a better hope.</hi> All these here named were not high priests; for, in the time of the judges, that dignity was, upon some occasion or other, brought into the family of Ithamar, of which Eli was; but in Zadok it returned again to the right line. Of Azariah it is here said (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.10">v. 10</reference>), <hi type="italic">He it is that executed the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built.</hi> It is supposed that this was that Azariah who bravely opposed the presumption of king Uzziah when he invaded the priest's office (<reference osisRef="2Chr.26.17-2Chr.26.18">2 Chron. xxvi. 17, 18</reference>), though he ventured his neck by so doing. This was done like a priest, like one that was truly zealous for his God. He that thus boldly maintained and defended the priest's office, and made good its barriers against such a daring insult, might well be said to <hi type="italic">execute it;</hi> and this honour is put upon him for it; while Urijah, one of his successors, for a base compliance with King Ahaz, in building him an idolatrous altar, has the disgrace put upon him of being left out of this genealogy, as perhaps some others are. But some think that this remark upon this Azariah should have been added to his grandfather of the same name (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.9">v. 9</reference>), who was the son of Ahimaaz, and that he was the priest who first officiated in Solomon's temple. 3. Some other of the families of the Levites are here accounted for. One of the families of Gershom (that of Libni) is here drawn down as far as Samuel, who had the honour of a prophet added to that of a Levite. One of the families of Merari (that of Mahli) is likewise drawn down for several descents, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.29-1Chr.6.30">v. 29, 30</reference>.

(<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1015.)</title> <div sID="gen7680" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">31</hi> And these <hi type="italic">are they</hi> whom David set over the service of song in the house of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , after that the ark had rest. <hi type="super">32</hi> And they ministered before the dwelling place of the tabernacle of the congregation with singing, until Solomon had built the house of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> in Jerusalem: and <hi type="italic">then</hi> they waited on their office according to their order. <hi type="super">33</hi> And these <hi type="italic">are</hi> they that waited with their children. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman a singer, the son of Joel, the son of Shemuel, <hi type="super">34</hi> The son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah, <hi type="super">35</hi> The son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai, <hi type="super">36</hi> The son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah, <hi type="super">37</hi> The son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, <hi type="super">38</hi> The son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel. <hi type="super">39</hi> And his brother Asaph, who stood on his right hand, <hi type="italic">even</hi> Asaph the son of Berachiah, the son of Shimea, <hi type="super">40</hi> The son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchiah, <hi type="super">41</hi> The son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah, <hi type="super">42</hi> The son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei, <hi type="super">43</hi> The son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi. <hi type="super">44</hi> And their brethren the sons of Merari <hi type="italic">stood</hi> on the left hand: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch, <hi type="super">45</hi> The son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah, <hi type="super">46</hi> The son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shamer, <hi type="super">47</hi> The son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi. <hi type="super">48</hi> Their brethren also the Levites <hi type="italic">were</hi> appointed unto all manner of service of the tabernacle of the house of God. <hi type="super">49</hi> But Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, <hi type="italic">and were appointed</hi> for all the work of the <hi type="italic">place</hi> most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded. <hi type="super">50</hi> And these <hi type="italic">are</hi> the sons of Aaron; Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son, <hi type="super">51</hi> Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son, <hi type="super">52</hi> Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son, <hi type="super">53</hi> Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son. <div eID="gen7680" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7681" type="x-p"/> When the Levites were first ordained in the wilderness much of the work then appointed them lay in carrying and taking care of the tabernacle and the utensils of it, while they were in their march through the wilderness. In David's time their number was increased; and, though the greater part of them was dispersed all the nation over, to teach the people the good knowledge of the Lord, yet those that attended the house of God were so numerous that there was not constant work for them all; and therefore David, by special commission and direction from God, new-modelled the Levites, as we shall find in the latter part of this book. Here we are told what the work was which he assigned them. <div eID="gen7681" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7682" type="x-p"/> I. Singing-work, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.31">v. 31</reference>. David was raised up on high to be the sweet psalmist of Israel (<reference osisRef="2Sam.23.1">2 Sam. xxiii. 1</reference>), not only to pen psalms, but to appoint the singing of them in the house of the Lord (not so much because he was musical as because he was devout), and this he did <hi type="italic">after that the ark had rest.</hi> While that was in captivity, obscure, and unsettled, the harps were hung upon the willow-trees: singing was then thought unseasonable (when the bridegroom is taken away they shall fast); but the harps being resumed, and the songs revived, at the bringing up of the ark, they were continued afterwards. For we should rejoice as much in the prolonging of our spiritual privileges as in the restoring of them. When the service of the ark was much superseded by its rest they had other work cut out for them (for Levites should never be idle) and were employed in the service of song. Thus when the people of God come to the rest which remains for them above they shall take leave of all their burdens and be employed in everlasting songs. These singers kept up that service in the tabernacle till the temple was built, and then they <hi type="italic">waited on their office</hi> there, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.32">v. 32</reference>. When they came to that stately magnificent house they kept as close both to their office and to their order as they had done in the tabernacle. It is a pity that the preferment of the Levites should ever make them remiss in their business. We have here an account of the three great masters who were employed in the service of the sacred song, with their respective families; for they <hi type="italic">waited with their children,</hi> that is, such as descended from them or were allied to them, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.33">v. 33</reference>. Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were the three that were appointed to this service, one of each of the three houses of the Levites, that there might be an equality in the distribution of this work and honour, and that every one might know his post, such an admirable order was there in this choir service. 1. Of the house of Kohath was Heman with his family (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.33">v. 33</reference>), a man of a sorrowful spirit, if it be the same Heman that penned the <reference osisRef="Ps.88.1-Ps.88.18">88th psalm</reference>, and yet a singer. He was the grandson of Samuel the prophet, the son of Joel, of whom it is said that <hi type="italic">he walked not in the ways of Samuel</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Sam.8.2-1Sam.8.3">1 Sam. viii. 2, 3</reference>); but it seems, though the son did not, the grandson did. Thus does the blessing entailed on the seed of the upright sometimes pass over one generation and fasten upon the next. And this Heman, though the grandson of that mighty prince, did not think it below him to be a precentor in the house of God. David himself was willing to be a door-keeper. Rather we may look upon this preferment of the grandson in the church as a recompense for the humble modest resignation which the grandfather made of his authority in the state. Many such ways God has of making up his people's losses and balancing their disgraces. Perhaps David, in making Heman the chief, had some respect to his old friend Samuel. 2. Of the house of Gershom was Asaph, called <hi type="italic">his brother,</hi> because in the same office and of the same tribe, though of another family. He was posted on Heman's right hand in the choir, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.39">v. 39</reference>. Several of the psalms bear his name, being either penned by him or tuned by him as the chief musician. It is plain that he was the penman of some psalms; for we read of those that praised the Lord in the words of David and of Asaph. He was a seer as well as a singer, <reference osisRef="2Chr.29.30">2 Chron. xxix. 30</reference>. His pedigree is traced up here, through names utterly unknown, as high as Levi, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.39-1Chr.6.43">v. 39-43</reference>. 3. Of the house of Merari was Ethan (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.44">v. 44</reference>), who was appointed to Heman's left hand. His pedigree is also traced up to Levi, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.47">v. 47</reference>. If these were the Heman and Ethan that penned the <reference osisRef="Ps.88.1-Ps.89.52">88th and 89th psalms</reference>, there appears no reason here why they should be called <hi type="italic">Ezrahites</hi> (see the titles of those psalms), as there does why those should be called so who are mentioned <reference osisRef="1Chr.2.6">ch. ii. 6</reference>, and who were the sons of Zerah. <div eID="gen7682" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7683" type="x-p"/> II. There was serving-work, abundance of service to be done <hi type="italic">in the tabernacle of the house of God</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.48">v. 48</reference>), to provide water and fuel,—to wash and sweep, and carry out ashes,—to kill, and flay, and boil the sacrifices; and to all such services there were Levites appointed, those of other families, or perhaps those that were not fit to be singers, that had either no good voice or no good ear. <hi type="italic">As every one has received the gift, so let him minister.</hi> Those that could not sing must not therefore be laid aside as good for nothing; though they were not fit for that service, there was other service they might be useful in. <div eID="gen7683" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7684" type="x-p"/> III. There was sacrificing-work, and that was to be done by the priests only, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.49">v. 49</reference>. They only were to sprinkle the blood and burn the incense; as for <hi type="italic">the work of the most holy place,</hi> that was to be done by the high priest only. Each had his work, and they both needed one another and both helped one another in it. Concerning the work of the priests we are here told, 1. What was the end they were to have in their eye. They were to <hi type="italic">make an atonement for Israel,</hi> to mediate between the people and God; not to magnify and enrich themselves, but to serve the public. They were <hi type="italic">ordained for men.</hi> 2. What was the rule they were to have in their eye. They presided in God's house, yet must do as they were bidden, according to all that God commanded. That law the highest are subject to.
entries.1676f7cf8960636eff3928dfddce0bc6b3e7eca2: <div eID="gen7684" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Cities of the Levites. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1444.)</title> <div sID="gen7685" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">54</hi> Now these <hi type="italic">are</hi> their dwelling places throughout their castles in their coasts, of the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites: for theirs was the lot. <hi type="super">55</hi> And they gave them Hebron in the land of Judah, and the suburbs thereof round about it. <hi type="super">56</hi> But the fields of the city, and the villages thereof, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh. <hi type="super">57</hi> And to the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of Judah, <hi type="italic">namely,</hi> Hebron, <hi type="italic">the city</hi> of refuge, and Libnah with her suburbs, and Jattir, and Eshtemoa, with their suburbs, <hi type="super">58</hi> And Hilen with her suburbs, Debir with her suburbs, <hi type="super">59</hi> And Ashan with her suburbs, and Beth-shemesh with her suburbs: <hi type="super">60</hi> And out of the tribe of Benjamin; Geba with her suburbs, and Alemeth with her suburbs, and Anathoth with her suburbs. All their cities throughout their families <hi type="italic">were</hi> thirteen cities. <hi type="super">61</hi> And unto the sons of Kohath, <hi type="italic">which were</hi> left of the family of that tribe, <hi type="italic">were cities given</hi> out of the half tribe, <hi type="italic">namely, out of</hi> the half <hi type="italic">tribe</hi> of Manasseh, by lot, ten cities. <hi type="super">62</hi> And to the sons of Gershom throughout their families out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities. <hi type="super">63</hi> Unto the sons of Merari <hi type="italic">were given</hi> by lot, throughout their families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities. <hi type="super">64</hi> And the children of Israel gave to the Levites <hi type="italic">these</hi> cities with their suburbs. <hi type="super">65</hi> And they gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities, which are called by <hi type="italic">their</hi> names. <hi type="super">66</hi> And <hi type="italic">the residue</hi> of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their coasts out of the tribe of Ephraim. <hi type="super">67</hi> And they gave unto them, <hi type="italic">of</hi> the cities of refuge, Shechem in mount Ephraim with her suburbs; <hi type="italic">they gave</hi> also Gezer with her suburbs, <hi type="super">68</hi> And Jokmeam with her suburbs, and Beth-horon with her suburbs, <hi type="super">69</hi> And Aijalon with her suburbs, and Gath-rimmon with her suburbs: <hi type="super">70</hi> And out of the half tribe of Manasseh; Aner with her suburbs, and Bileam with her suburbs, for the family of the remnant of the sons of Kohath. <hi type="super">71</hi> Unto the sons of Gershom <hi type="italic">were given</hi> out of the family of the half tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with her suburbs, and Ashtaroth with her suburbs: <hi type="super">72</hi> And out of the tribe of Issachar; Kedesh with her suburbs, Daberath with her suburbs, <hi type="super">73</hi> And Ramoth with her suburbs, and Anem with her suburbs: <hi type="super">74</hi> And out of the tribe of Asher; Mashal with her suburbs, and Abdon with her suburbs, <hi type="super">75</hi> And Hukok with her suburbs, and Rehob with her suburbs: <hi type="super">76</hi> And out of the tribe of Naphtali; Kedesh in Galilee with her suburbs, and Hammon with her suburbs, and Kirjathaim with her suburbs. <hi type="super">77</hi> Unto the rest of the children of Merari <hi type="italic">were given</hi> out of the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmon with her suburbs, Tabor with her suburbs: <hi type="super">78</hi> And on the other side Jordan by Jericho, on the east side of Jordan, <hi type="italic">were given them</hi> out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness with her suburbs, and Jahzah with her suburbs, <hi type="super">79</hi> Kedemoth also with her suburbs, and Mephaath with her suburbs: <hi type="super">80</hi> And out of the tribe of Gad; Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbs, and Mahanaim with her suburbs, <hi type="super">81</hi> And Heshbon with her suburbs, and Jazer with her suburbs. <div eID="gen7685" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7686" type="x-p"/> We have here an account of the Levites' cities. They are here called their <hi type="italic">castles</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.54">v. 54</reference>), not only because walled and fortified, and well guarded by the country (for it is the interest of every nation to protect its ministers), but because they and their possessions were, in a particular manner, the care of the divine providence: as God was their portion, so God was their protection; and a cottage will be a castle to those that abide under the shadow of the Almighty. This account is much the same with that which we had, <reference osisRef="Josh.21.1-Josh.21.45">Josh. xxi.</reference> We need not be critical in comparing them (what good will it do us?) nor will it do any hurt to the credit of the holy scripture if the names of some of the places be not spelt just the same here as they were there. We know it is common for cities to have several names. <hi type="italic">Sarum</hi> and <hi type="italic">Salisbury, Salop</hi> and <hi type="italic">Shrewsbury,</hi> are more unlike than <hi type="italic">Hilen</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.58">v. 58</reference>) and <hi type="italic">Holon</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.15">Josh. xxi. 15</reference>), <hi type="italic">Ashan</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.59">v. 59</reference>) and <hi type="italic">Ain</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.16">Josh. xxi. 16</reference>), <hi type="italic">Alemeth</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.60">v. 60</reference>) and <hi type="italic">Almon</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.18">Josh. xxi. 18</reference>); and time changes names. We are only to observe that in this appointment of cities for the Levites God took care, 1. For the accomplishment of dying Jacob's prediction concerning this tribe, that it should be <hi type="italic">scattered in Israel,</hi> <reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Gen. xlix. 7</reference>. 2. For the diffusing of the knowledge of himself and his law to all parts of the land of Israel. Every tribe had Levites' cities in it; and so every room was furnished with a candle, so that none could be ignorant of his duty but it was either his own fault or the Levites'. 3. For a comfortable maintenance for those that ministered in holy things. Besides their tithes and offerings, they had glebe-lands and cities of their own to dwell in. Some of the most considerable cities of Israel fell to the Levites' lot. Every tribe had benefit by the Levites, and therefore every tribe must contribute to their support. <hi type="italic">Let him that is taught in the word communicate to him that teacheth,</hi> and do it cheerfully.  <chapter eID="1Chr.6"/> <div eID="gen7686" type="x-p"/>

Line of the Priests.<div eID="gen5261" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5262" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3675"/><hi type="bold">5. Uzzi--</hi>It is supposed that, in his days, the high priesthood was, for unrecorded reasons, transferred from Eleazar's family to Ithamar's, in which it continued for several generations. <div eID="gen5262" type="x-p"/>
entries.69bfc605b8c9750f8fc1eb872c86a5675ae3b868: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3676"/><div sID="gen5263" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3676"/><hi type="bold">10. he it is that executed the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem--</hi>It is doubtful whether the person in favor of whom this testimony is borne be Johanan or Azariah. If the former, he is the same as Jehoiada, who rendered important public services (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.11.1-2Kgs.11.20">2Ki 11:1-20</reference>); if the latter, it refers to the worthy and independent part he acted in resisting the unwarrantable encroachments of Uzziah (<reference osisRef="2Chr.26.17">2Ch 26:17</reference>).<div eID="gen5263" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5264" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem--</hi>described in this particular manner to distinguish it from the second temple, which was in existence at the time when this history was written. <div eID="gen5264" type="x-p"/>
entries.6ba53051b76ec2a9bc4d7d435e6e524ed71cf0d1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3677"/><div sID="gen5265" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3677"/><hi type="bold">14. Azariah begat Seraiah--</hi>He filled the supreme pontifical office at the destruction of Jerusalem, and, along with his deputy and others, he was executed by Nebuchadnezzar's orders at Riblah (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.18">2Ki 25:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.21">21</reference>). The line of high priests, under the first temple, which from Zadok amounted to twelve, terminated with him. <div eID="gen5265" type="x-p"/>
entries.3d2e770384de30a47f4b193d6aa46d5d56821a47: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3678"/><div sID="gen5266" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3678"/><hi type="bold">16-48. The sons of Levi; Gershom, &c.--</hi>This repetition (see <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference>) is made, as the historian here begins to trace the genealogy of the Levitical families who were not priests. The list is a long one, comprising the chiefs or heads of their several families until David's reign, who made a new and different classification of them by courses. <div eID="gen5266" type="x-p"/>
entries.87d4cb74f20d465da004570aa7585a0c4653bea2: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3688"/><div sID="gen5278" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3688"/><hi type="bold">49. But Aaron and his sons offered, &c.--</hi>The office and duties of the high priests having been already described, the names of those who successively filled that important office are recorded. <div eID="gen5278" type="x-p"/>
entries.106bc08d853cdbfab07e05eee4745adb3a712186: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3689"/><div sID="gen5279" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3689"/><hi type="bold">60. thirteen cities--</hi>No more than eleven are named here; but two additional ones are mentioned (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.16">Jos 21:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Josh.21.17">17</reference>), which makes up the thirteen. <div eID="gen5279" type="x-p"/>
entries.7219e17dcd971729e59fd16214805137c1b9fe61: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3690"/><div sID="gen5280" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3690"/><hi type="bold">61. unto the sons of Kohath, which were left--</hi>that is, in addition to the priests belonging to the same family and tribe of Levi.<div eID="gen5280" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5281" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">by lot, ten cities--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Josh.21.26">Jos 21:26</reference>). The sacred historian gives an explanation (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.66">1Ch 6:66</reference>). Eight of these are mentioned, but only two of them are taken out of the half tribe of Manasseh (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.70">1Ch 6:70</reference>). The names of the other two are given (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.21">Jos 21:21</reference>), where full and detailed notices of these arrangements may be found. <div eID="gen5281" type="x-p"/>
entries.ee796860830c59a2176dbc37188e19dee88d2d83: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3691"/><div sID="gen5282" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3691"/><hi type="bold">62. to the sons of Gershom--</hi>Supply "the children of Israel gave." <div eID="gen5282" type="x-p"/>
entries.ab2b54d7f787e5df453c37d924fffc5e090f5ebc: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3692"/><div sID="gen5283" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3692"/><hi type="bold">67-81. they gave unto them of the cities of refuge--</hi>The names of the cities given here are considerably different from those applied to them (<reference osisRef="Josh.21.13-Josh.21.19">Jos 21:13-19</reference>). In the lapse of centuries, and from the revolutions of society, changes might have been expected to take place in the form or dialectic pronunciation of the names of those cities; and this will sufficiently account for the variations that are found in the lists as enumerated here and in an earlier book. As to these cities themselves that were assigned to the Levites, they were widely remote and separated--partly in fulfilment of Jacob's prophecy (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.7">Ge 49:7</reference>), and partly that the various districts of the country might obtain a competent supply of teachers who might instruct the people in the knowledge, and animate them to the observance, of a law which had so important a bearing on the promotion both of their private happiness and their national prosperity. <chapter eID="1Chr.6"/>

entries.7eddb52b2f57ab1457f50b17c1f2761bdb614642: <div eID="gen13488" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen13489" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen13490" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen13490" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen13489" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen13491" type="x-p"/> The genealogy of Levi and Aaron, vv. 1-30. The offices of the priests and Levites, vv. 31-53. The cities assigned them, vv. 54-81. <div eID="gen13491" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13492" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen13492" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13493" type="x-p"/> The sons of Levi - It has been well remarked that the genealogy of Levi is given here more ample and correct than that of any of the others. <div eID="gen13493" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13494" type="x-p"/> And this is perhaps an additional proof that the author was a priest, felt much for the priesthood, and took care to give the genealogy of the Levitical and sacerdotal families, from the most correct tables; for with such tables we may presume he was intimately acquainted.
entries.28b26ad32dbb2175e7d12c58e10471c11f1c616d: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen13494" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13495" type="x-p"/> Eleazar begat Phinehas - As the high priesthood continued in this family for a long time, the sacred historian confines himself to this chiefly, omitting Nadab and Abihu, and even the family of Ithamar.
entries.fc8c9232150c64848f46dab558c893c011119c21: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen13495" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13496" type="x-p"/> Ahitub begat Zadok - Through this person the high priesthood came again into the family of Eleazar.
entries.afff8c9282a686782bf18c238fe5f864aee7527a: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen13496" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13497" type="x-p"/> Johanan - Supposed to be the same as Jehoiada. <div eID="gen13497" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13498" type="x-p"/> Executed the priest's office - Probably this refers to the dignified manner in which Azariah opposed King Uzziah, who wished to invade the priest's office, and offer incense in the temple. See <reference osisRef="2Chr.26.17">2Chr 26:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.26.18">2Chr 26:18</reference>.
entries.ba5bb1d88523cd08edeb3a36ac59ac4ed1dd3059: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen13498" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13499" type="x-p"/> Seraiah - He was put to death by Nebuchadnezzar, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.18">2Kgs 25:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.21">2Kgs 25:21</reference>.
entries.523b15070492e6fe2462ceed98526a35a0b70f8d: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen13499" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13500" type="x-p"/> Korah - See the history of this man, and his rebellion, Numbers 16:1-33.
entries.4ebc9a9a9e2ecc9832846a5f985c91593884c71d: <hi type="bold">Verse 28</hi> <div eID="gen13500" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13501" type="x-p"/> The first-born Vashni, and Abiah - There is a great mistake in this verse: in <reference osisRef="1Sam.8.2">1Sam 8:2</reference> we read, Now the name of his (Samuel's) first-born was Joel; and the name of his second Abiah. The word יואל Joel is lost out of the text in this place, and ושני vesheni, which signifies the second, and which refers to Abiah, is made here into a proper name. The Septuagint, Vulgate, and Chaldee, copy this blunder; but the Syriac and Arabic read as in <reference osisRef="1Sam.8.2">1Sam 8:2</reference>. The MSS. have all copied the corrupted Hebrew in this place. Jarchi labors to restore the true reading, and yet preserve the integrity of the text, by paraphrasing thus: "And the second, (ושני vesheni), in respect of the first, he was Abiah; and the second, in respect of Abiah, he was Joel." <div eID="gen13501" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13502" type="x-p"/> These, Joel and Abiah, were the two sons of Samuel, who administered justice so badly that the people, being oppressed, began to murmur, and demanded a king. See <reference osisRef="1Sam.8.1">1Sam 8:1</reference>, etc.
entries.4046757d2a6b29e782f97615add429d2c3f20bb6: <hi type="bold">Verse 31</hi> <div eID="gen13502" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13503" type="x-p"/> After that the ark had rest - The Targum says, "These are they whom David set over the service of the singing, in the house of the sanctuary, or tabernacle of the Lord, at the time in which the ark was brought into it;" that is, when it was brought from the house of Obed-edom.
entries.d63a9a28337bc0c122fadac12e223a399f4f04d5: <hi type="bold">Verse 32</hi> <div eID="gen13503" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13504" type="x-p"/> According to their order - This order is specified below.
entries.bc669f0f71b408455e75be22d401e83a1b9088dc: <hi type="bold">Verse 39</hi> <div eID="gen13504" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13505" type="x-p"/> Asaph - This person, with Heman, the sons of Kora, Ethan, Jeduthun, etc., are celebrated in these books, and in the Psalms, for their skill in singing, and the part they performed in the public worship of God. <div eID="gen13505" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13506" type="x-p"/> It is very likely that their singing was only a kind of recitative or chanting, such as we still find in the synagogues. It does not appear that God had especially appointed these singers, much less any musical instruments, (the silver trumpets excepted), to be employed in his service. Musical instruments in the house of God are, at least under the Gospel, repugnant to the spirit of Christianity, and tend not a little to corrupt the worship of God. Those who are fond of music in the theater are fond of it in the house of God when they go thither; and some, professing Christianity, set up such a spurious worship in order to draw people to hear the Gospel! This is doing evil that good may come of it; and by this means, light and trifling people are introduced into the Church of Christ, and when in, are generally very troublesome, hard to be pleased, and difficult to be saved.
entries.f7cd90b828c741613795d860fcd8f9e22060bbd4: <hi type="bold">Verse 50</hi> <div eID="gen13506" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13507" type="x-p"/> These are the sons of Aaron - We have already had a list of these, (see <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.3-1Chr.6.16">1Chr 6:3-16</reference>); this is a second, but less extensive, and is a proof that the writer of this book had several lists before him, from which he borrowed as he judged proper.
entries.acc9b321820545c4d7249ba957cbf927718da605: <hi type="bold">Verse 54</hi> <div eID="gen13507" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13508" type="x-p"/> Theirs was the lot - All the tribes and families obtained their respective inheritances by lot, but to the sons of Aaron was the first lot; and so the Syriac and Arabic have understood this place. The first lot, says Jarchi, fell to Judah, that they might give to the priests and the Levites the cities marked below. See an account of the possessions of the priests and Levites, <reference osisRef="Jos.20.1-Jos.20.9">Jos 20:1-9</reference>, 21.
entries.9445f928a4dd64af0df57a353e5baaf04f481da9: <hi type="bold">Verse 60</hi> <div eID="gen13508" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13509" type="x-p"/> All their cities - were thirteen - But there are only eleven reckoned here, Gibeon and Juttah being omitted, and the names of some of the others changed. None of the versions give the full number of names, although they all give the whole sum thirteen.
entries.59223b17d707c1f9ecf4a178e409495861752bb8: <hi type="bold">Verse 65</hi> <div eID="gen13509" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13510" type="x-p"/> Which are called by their names - Probably each family gave its own name to the city that fell to its lot.
entries.8cd4f53423c03dea68b02dd600efa591195c995e: <hi type="bold">Verse 69</hi> <div eID="gen13510" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13511" type="x-p"/> Aijalon with her suburbs - There are the two cities wanting here, Eltekeh and Gibethon. See <reference osisRef="Jos.21.23">Jos 21:23</reference>.
entries.548816c7a40cee41e21870048559b7a23a8190f2: <hi type="bold">Verse 71</hi> <div eID="gen13511" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13512" type="x-p"/> We shall see from <reference osisRef="Jos.21.28">Jos 21:28</reference>, etc., that several of these cities have different names. <div eID="gen13512" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13513" type="x-p"/> How barren to us is this register, both of incident and interest! and yet, as barren rocks and sandy deserts make integral and necessary parts of the globe; so do these genealogical tables make necessary parts of the history of providence and grace in the maintenance of truth, and the establishment of the Church of Christ. Therefore no one that fears God will either despise or lightly esteem them.  <chapter eID="1Chr.6"/> <div eID="gen13513" type="x-p"/>

entries.5aa2264317b61eb234bae8c16a66ed5effe95b17: <div eID="gen5634" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">The Families of Levi, and Their Cities - 1 Chronicles 6 1 Chronicles 6 (Hebrew_Bible_5:27-6:66).</title> <div sID="gen5635" type="x-p"/> As to the tribe of Levi, we have several communications: (1.) the genealogy of the high-priestly family of Aaron, down to Jehozadak, who was led away into exile by Nebuchadnezzar (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1-1Chr.6.15">1Ch 6:1-15</reference>); (2.) a short register of the families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, which does not extend far into later times (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16-1Chr.6.30">1Ch 6:16-30</reference>); (3.) the genealogies of the musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan (1 Chron 6:31-47), with remarks on the service of the other Levites (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.48">1Ch 6:48</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.49">1Ch 6:49</reference>); (4.) a register of the high priests from Eleazar to Ahimaaz the son of Zadok (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.50-1Chr.6.53">1Ch 6:50-53</reference>), with a register of the cities of the Levites (1 Chron 6:54-81). If we look into these genealogies and registers, we see, both from a repetition of a part of the genealogy of the high priest (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.50-1Chr.6.53">1Ch 6:50-53</reference>), and also from the name of the eldest son of Levi appearing in two different forms - in 1Ch 6:1. Gershon; in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16-1Chr.6.17">1Ch 6:16-17</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.20">1Ch 6:20</reference>, etc., Gershom - that the register in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1-1Chr.6.15">1Ch 6:1-15</reference> is drawn from another source than the registers in 1 Chron 6, which, with the exception of the genealogies of David’s chief musicians, are throughout fragmentary, and in parts corrupt, and were most probably found by the author of the Chronicle in this defective state. <div eID="gen5635" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5636" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1-1Chr.6.15">1Ch 6:1-15</reference> (Hebrew_Bible_5:27-41). <hi type="italic">The family of Aaron, or the high-priestly line of Aaron, to the time of the Babylonian exile.</hi> - <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference>-3. In order to exhibit the connection of Aharon (or Aaron) with the patriarch Levi, the enumeration begins with the three sons of Levi, who are given in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference> as in <reference osisRef="Gen.46.11">Gen 46:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.6.16">Exo 6:16</reference>, and in other passages. Of Levi’s grandchildren, only the four sons of Kohath (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.2">1Ch 6:2</reference>) are noticed; and of these, again, Amram is the only one whose descendants - Aaron, Moses, and Miriam - are named (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.3">1Ch 6:3</reference>); and thereafter only Aaron’s sons are introduced, in order that the enumeration of his family in the high-priestly line of Eleazar might follow. With <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.2">1Ch 6:2</reference> cf. <reference osisRef="Exod.1.18">Exo 1:18</reference>, and on <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.34">1Ch 6:34</reference> see the commentary on Exo 6:20. With the sons of Aaron (<hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="1Chr.6.44">1Ch 6:44</reference></hi>) compare besides <reference osisRef="Exod.6.23">Exo 6:23</reference>, also Num 3:2-4, and <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.1">1Ch 24:1</reference>-2. As Nadab and Abihu were slain when they offered strange fire before Jahve (Lev 10:1.), Aaron’s race was continued only by his sons Eleazar and Ithamar. After Aaron’s death, his eldest son Eleazar was chosen by God to be his successor in the high priest’s office, and thus the line of Eleazar came into possession of the high-priestly dignity.
entries.759b11797a59fa52624c2cf47ad9a94c31630be8: <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16-1Chr.6.81">1Ch 6:16-81</reference> (Hebrew_Bible_Ch. 6). The families and cities of the Levites. - Vv. 1-34. Register of the families of the Levites. - This is introduced by an enumeration of the sons and grandsons of Levi (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16-1Chr.6.19">1Ch 6:16-19</reference>), which is followed by lists of families in six lines of descent: (<hi type="italic">a</hi>) the descendants of Gershon (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.20-1Chr.6.21">1Ch 6:20-21</reference>), of Kohath (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.22-1Chr.6.28">1Ch 6:22-28</reference>), and of Merari (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.29-1Chr.6.30">1Ch 6:29-30</reference>); and (<hi type="italic">b</hi>) the genealogies of David’s chief musicians (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.31">1Ch 6:31</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.32">1Ch 6:32</reference>), of Heman the Kohathite (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.33-1Chr.6.38">1Ch 6:33-38</reference>), of Asaph the Gershonite (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.39-1Chr.6.43">1Ch 6:39-43</reference>), and of Ethan the Merarite (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.44-1Chr.6.47">1Ch 6:44-47</reference>); and in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.48">1Ch 6:48</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.49">1Ch 6:49</reference>, some notes as to the service performed by the other Levites and the priests are added. (Hebrew_Bible_6:1-4). The sons of Levi are in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference> again enumerated as in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference>; then in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16-1Chr.6.22">1Ch 6:16-22</reference> the sons of these three sons, i.e., the grandsons of Levi, are introduced, while in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference> only the sons of Kohath are mentioned. The only object of this enumeration is to make quite clear the descent of the Levitic families which follow. The name of the first son of Levi is in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.16">1Ch 6:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.17">1Ch 6:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.20">1Ch 6:20</reference>, etc. of this chapter גּרשׁם, which was the name of Moses’ son, cf. 1Ch 23:15.; whereas in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.1">1Ch 6:1</reference> and in the Pentateuch we find a different pronunciation, viz., גּרשׁון. The names of Levi’s grandsons in <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.17-1Chr.6.22">1Ch 6:17-22</reference> coincide with the statements of the Pentateuch, <reference osisRef="Exod.6.17-Exod.6.19">Exo 6:17-19</reference>, and Num 3:17-20, cf. Num 26:57. Bertheau and other commentators consider the words in <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="1Chr.6.17">1Ch 6:17</reference></hi>, “and these are the families of Levi according to their fathers,” to be a “concluding subscription” to the statements of <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.15-1Chr.6.17">1Ch 6:15-17</reference>, and would remove ו before אלּה, as not compatible with this supposition. But in this he is wrong: for although the similar statement in <reference osisRef="Exod.6.20">Exo 6:20</reference> is a subscription, yet it is in Num 3:20 a superscription, and must in our verse also be so understood; for otherwise the enumeration of the descendants of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, which follows, would be brought in very abruptly, without any connecting particle, and the ו before אלּה points to the same conclusion.
